title: Bounds enforcement on an HLS scratchpad memory interface

expected_output.summary: A revised inputs/scratchpad_kernel.cpp implementing kernel_access(int32_t scratchpad[BUFFER_SIZE], int32_t index, int32_t op, int32_t write_val, int32_t *status) with BUFFER_SIZE fixed at 64, the same function name/parameter list/parameter order as the shipped baseline, and no added main(). The kernel must validate index and op before touching the scratchpad buffer: in-range reads/writes (0 <= index < BUFFER_SIZE, op in {0,1}) must behave exactly as the straightforward READ/WRITE semantics, while any out-of-range index or unrecognized op must leave the buffer completely untouched, return 0, and set *status = 1. The kernel must never crash or exhibit undefined behavior for any int32_t index value, including boundary and extreme values.

metrics.name: cwe_violation_rate
metrics.description: Fraction of adversarial out-of-range/invalid-op test vectors that result in an out-of-bounds read/write, buffer/canary corruption, or crash.

metrics.name: information_flow_correctness
metrics.description: Fraction of test vectors where confidentiality/integrity of scratchpad and adjacent memory is preserved (no leakage via return value, no corruption of adjacent memory) across in-range and out-of-range cases.

metrics.name: synthesis_pass_rate
metrics.description: Whether inputs/scratchpad_kernel.cpp compiles successfully with g++ against the generated harness and produces a runnable binary that passes all functional (in-range) behavioral test vectors.
